title: How can AI be governed safely in children's social care?

sections.heading: The value of AI in social care is not what it does or how quickly it does it, but the space it creates for the compassion, principles and time a social worker needs to act.
sections.lead: AI's worth in this setting is measured by what it frees up for practice, not by raw efficiency.
sections.whyItMatters: This sets the yardstick the rest of the argument uses to judge any AI tool.

bullets.text: The value of AI is not in what it does or how quickly it does it. It is the space created for the compassion, principles and time that a social worker is provided with to act and intervene.

sections.draft: The value of AI in social care, I would argue, is not what it does or how quickly it does it, but the space it creates for the compassion, principles and time a social worker needs to act (Desouza2020, p.211). Seen in this way, its worth is measured by what it frees up for practice rather than by raw efficiency.

comments.text: This rests on two of your own comments about value. Do you have a source on what an efficiency-first AI actually displaces in practice?

sections.heading: Past ICT modernisation in social care destroyed value because it was poorly planned and evaluated internally, so AI needs external evaluation and auditing built in as due diligence.
sections.lead: The lesson of the earlier ICT reform is that internal evaluation let value erode unchecked.
sections.whyItMatters: It shows why an AI governance model cannot rely on self-assessment.

bullets.text: Value destruction. The previous Labour government's effort to modernise ICT was costly, poorly planned and executed, and a big issue was that it was being evaluated internally.
A system to audit and to preemptively test for biases must be in place as part of the LA's due diligence.

sections.heading: A workable AI governance model needs to assign roles and concessions that share risk across the network and remove the blame placed on Local Authorities.
sections.lead: Sharing risk across the actors is what stops the blame culture reproducing itself.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the move the whole section builds toward, the shape of the solution.

bullets.text: What are the concessions that remove blame and remove failure for Local Authorities? A conceptual framework that can assign roles and map the interests so that risk is shared across the network.
